en: Jupiter's diameter is about 143,000 kilometers, making it more than eleven times wider than Earth.
The Moon orbits Earth at an average distance of 384,400 kilometers, taking light just 1.3 seconds to travel.
Earth's oceanic crust is only about 5 kilometers thick, while the continental crust can be up to 70 kilometers thick.
Approximately 97 percent of Earth's water is salty ocean water, leaving just 3 percent as freshwater for drinking and farming.
The Sun is so massive that approximately one million Earths could fit inside its glowing, spherical surface.
In the Philippines, a Super Typhoon is officially classified as having maximum sustained winds of at least 185 kilometers per hour.
Clay particles are the smallest soil type at under 0.002 millimeters, whereas sand particles are the largest at up to 2 millimeters.
Diamond is the hardest natural mineral on Earth, scoring a perfect 10 on the ten-point Mohs hardness scale.
Almost all Earth's weather occurs in the troposphere, the lowest atmospheric layer that extends about 12 kilometers above the surface.
Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system, with surface temperatures reaching a scorching 465 degrees Celsius.
Earth rotates at roughly 1,670 kilometers per hour at the equator, completing one full spin every 24 hours.
Deep-focus earthquakes occur at subduction zones, originating up to 700 kilometers below the Earth's surface.
